To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the SDPclust approach can predict specificity of a protein to a ligand, even if the ligand is not known, by analyzing the protein sequence only.
we have developed a method for identification of protein specificity determinants that is robust to phylogenetic noise.

the specificity of proteins to a binding partner can be predicted by the analysis of the protein sequence alone and that the SDPclust method is a powerful tool for identification of protein subfamilies and prediction of the specificity determinants.
In summary, our research is concerned with
development of an automated approach for the identification of functional subfamilies of proteins, which is based on the analysis of the amino acid sequence of proteins.
the development of a novel approach to the problem of the prediction of specificity in a phylogenetically independent manner.
development of an automated approach to identification of functional subfamilies of proteins and the identification of specificity-determinant positions.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
SDPclust can be used for the identification of specificity groups in proteins and for prediction of specificity-determined residues.
SDPclust performs better than any of the existing methods in the prediction of the specificity determinants and the functional subfamilies.
SDPclust provides a novel, statistically robust approach for the identification of specificity determinations in proteins.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

SDPclust provides a powerful tool for the identification of protein subfamilies and specificity determinants, and can be used for the prediction of the binding partners for a protein of unknown specificity.
we have created a method that is capable of identifying specificity determinants for proteins with unknown specificity and of grouping together proteins that share the same specificity.
SDPclust can identify functional subfamilies in a phylogenetic independent manner and can predict SDPs with an accuracy of 70% and above.
The main takeaway from our work is that
SDPclust can identify functional groups that are not necessarily phylogenetically related.
the identification of functional subfamilies is not a separate task from the prediction of specificity, but rather is the same task.
the identification of specificity determinating sites is a much more difficult task than the identification of functional subfamilies, and that the two tasks should be treated separately.
